# Data files

This folder contains raw source data, intermediate results, and cached outputs
used by the scripts in the project root (`analyze_animal_deaths.qmd`,
`analyze_comments_llm.R`, `analyze_comments_nrc.R`). Files fall into three
groups: **raw inputs** (downloaded, not generated by any script here),
**pipeline outputs** (generated by `analyze_animal_deaths.qmd`), and **comment
analysis outputs** (generated by `analyze_comments_llm.R` /
`analyze_comments_nrc.R`). Most generated files are cached — the scripts check
`file.exists()` before regenerating them, so delete a file if you want it
rebuilt from scratch.

## Raw inputs (downloaded, not generated)

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `imdb_movies_5000.csv` | Top 5000 movies from IMDB. [Source](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/tiagoadrianunes/imdb-top-5000-movies). Includes IMDB ID (`tconst`), title, year, rating, genres, etc. |
| `imdb_tvseries_5000.csv` | Top 5000 TV series from IMDB. [Source](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/tiagoadrianunes/imdb-top-5000-tv-shows). Same general schema as the movies file, plus `endYear`. |
| `dtdd_dog_cat_animal_items.csv` | Raw export from the [Does the Dog Die? (DTDD)](https://www.doesthedogdie.com/api) database of items (movies/TV shows) tagged under the "a dog dies," "a cat dies," and "an animal dies" topics, with vote totals (`yesSum`, `noSum`) and one representative comment per row. |
| `dtdd_dog_cat_animal_comments.csv` | Raw export of individual DTDD user comments for the same items/topics as above, with per-comment vote counts (`yes`, `no`, `voteSum`). This is the primary comment dataset used by `analyze_comments_llm.R` and `analyze_comments_nrc.R`. |

## Pipeline outputs (generated by `analyze_animal_deaths.qmd`)

For each of these, the `.csv` version is for human inspection and the `.rds`
version is what the analysis scripts read (faster, preserves types).

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `imdb_5000_dtdd_results.csv` / `.rds` | IMDB top-5000 movies matched to their DTDD entry (matched by IMDB ID), filtered to titles with a valid match, sufficient ratings, and matching release year. |
| `imdb_5000_dtdd_movie_details.csv` / `.rds` | Per-movie yes/no vote counts for the "a dog dies" / "a cat dies" / "an animal dies" topics, plus boolean columns `dog_death`, `cat_death`, `animal_death`. |
| `imdb_tvseries_5000_dtdd_results.csv` / `.rds` | TV series analogue of `imdb_5000_dtdd_results` |
| `imdb_tvseries_5000_dtdd_series_details.csv` / `.rds` | TV series analogue of `imdb_5000_dtdd_movie_details`. |

## Comment analysis outputs

### LLM scoring (`analyze_comments_llm.R`)

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `movie_comments_devset.csv` | 50 randomly sampled movie comments used to iteratively develop the LLM scoring prompt. LLM-scored only; no human labels. |
| `movie_comments_testset.csv` | 75 held-out movie comments, LLM-scored using the finalized prompt. Includes `on_screen`, `named_animal`, `plot_point` columns (dropped in later runs — see below). |
| `movie_comments_testset_humanscored.csv` | Same 75 test-set comments as above, manually scored for validating LLM agreement. |
| `movie_comments_llmscored.csv` | LLM scores for the full movie comment dataset (one comment per movie/topic, the single highest-voted comment). Columns: `death_confirmed`, `emotionality`, `intentionality`, `species` (the revised, reduced set of fields — `on_screen`, `named_animal`, and `plot_point` were dropped after dev/test evaluation showed poor LLM-human agreement). |
| `tv_comments_testset.csv` | 75 randomly sampled TV series comments, LLM-scored (same reduced variable set as above). |
| `tv_comments_testset_humanscored.csv` | Same TV test-set comments, manually scored for validating LLM agreement. |

Note: batch checkpoint files (`checkpoint_batch_*.csv`), produced while scoring
the full movie dataset in batches of 500, are deleted once
`movie_comments_llmscored.csv` is complete, but may reappear if a scoring run
is interrupted and needs to resume.
